sections.title: Form and range
sections.text: Bay laurel is an evergreen, dioecious tree or shrub native to the Mediterranean region and cultivated elsewhere. It can reach about 12 m.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: Its alternate, leathery, aromatic leaves are about 5.5–12 cm long and 1.8–3.2 cm wide. Small flowers grow in axillary umbels; the ripe oval drupes turn purplish black.

sections.title: Culinary use
sections.text: The leaves are used as a seasoning and are usually removed from the dish before eating. Bay laurel must be distinguished from other plants called laurel, some of which are poisonous.
